description: Slice-4 of the Codex backend epic: replace the informational codex spawn guard with a fail-closed codex auth preflight that aborts every codex dispatch before respawn-pane when codex is not authenticated, and retire the stale 'not yet wired (CAM-54)' notice.

userStories.title: Fail-closed codex auth preflight core (check + decision fn, retire stale notice)
userStories.description: As the cam supervisor, I need a centralized, injectable fail-closed codex auth preflight so that a codex-backed dispatch can be aborted early and actionably when codex is not authenticated, instead of drowning in 401/400 noise or relying on the old informational-only guard.
acceptanceCriteria: A shared decision fn (codexAuthPreflight) returns an abort result whose message names `codex login` when backend=codex and the injected auth-check reports unauthenticated. [oracle: bun test test/supervisor/codex-auth.test.ts]
codexAuthPreflight returns a proceed result (no abort) when backend=codex and the injected auth-check reports authenticated. [oracle: bun test]
codexAuthPreflight does no auth-check work and returns proceed when backend=claude (auth-check is never invoked on the claude path). [oracle: bun test]

When backend=codex and the resolved model is an obviously-claude alias (opus/sonnet/haiku), codexAuthPreflight aborts with an actionable message (this prevents the exact 400 observed live with the default opus/sonnet model names). [oracle: bun test]

The auth-check is an injectable function parameter (DI seam); the default production check reads ~/.codex/auth.json presence, not env vars (OPENAI_API_KEY/CODEX_API_KEY/CODEX_ACCESS_TOKEN), so tests never spawn the real codex binary. [oracle: grep -q 'auth.json' src/supervisor/codex-auth.ts]

The default auth-check's limitation is documented in-code: it detects the never-logged-in case but does NOT detect an expired-but-present token; no comment claims expiry-detection that is not implemented. [oracle: reviewer-judgment]

The literal string 'codex backend not yet wired (CAM-54)' no longer appears in any source path (the informational guard/notice is retired from emitSpawnResolution). [oracle: ! grep -rq 'codex backend not yet wired (CAM-54)' src/]
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck). [oracle: bun run typecheck]
Tests pass (bun test). [oracle: bun test]
Lint/static spine passes (bun run check:all). [oracle: bun run check:all]
userStories.notes: New module recommended: src/supervisor/codex-auth.ts (sibling to backend-adapter.ts) holding both the injectable codexAuthCheck (fs point-read of ~/.codex/auth.json via readFileSync/existsSync, a deliberate synchronous point-read carved out of the Bun-only rule) and the pure codexAuthPreflight({backend, model, authCheck}) decision fn. Edit src/logging/spawn-resolution.ts to remove CODEX_GUARD_NOTICE and the informational codex branch (emitSpawnResolution stays a pure emitter with a void return, so no call site breaks: keep this change additive/backward-compatible). Existing tests to update: test/logging/spawn-resolution.test.ts and test/logging/codex-guard.test.ts (they assert the old notice). Default model names are bare 'opus'/'sonnet' (src/config/models.ts DEFAULTS), which is why the claude-alias guard matters. Gotcha (from issue): `codex login status` reports 'Logged in' even with an EXPIRED token because it only checks auth.json presence, so auth.json-presence is a weak-but-cheap check equivalent to login-status; do not claim it catches expiry. Codex auth is ChatGPT-login via ~/.codex/auth.json, never env vars. Write any temp payloads to /tmp, never under .claude/. See patterns.md 'Spawn-resolution emitter pattern' and ADR-0047. Grep scripts/cam/pattern-records.jsonl for 'codex'/'preflight' before coding.

userStories.title: Wire fail-closed preflight at the 3 supervisor worker-dispatch sites
userStories.description: As the cam supervisor loop, I need the codex auth preflight enforced before every worker respawn-pane (implementer, reviewer, planner, auditor) so that an unauthenticated codex worker never gets dispatched and the loop halts with an actionable reason instead of a noisy 401/400 failure.
acceptanceCriteria: Each supervisor worker-dispatch site (loop.ts implementer, review.ts reviewer, plan-runner.ts planner and auditor) runs codexAuthPreflight (with the production auth-check) immediately before its respawn-pane call. [oracle: grep -q 'codexAuthPreflight' src/supervisor/loop.ts src/supervisor/review.ts src/supervisor/plan-runner.ts]

When backend=codex and the injected auth-check reports unauthenticated, the site returns a terminal blocked/error outcome carrying an actionable reason naming `codex login` and never calls respawn-pane (mirroring the existing container-mode fail-closed early-return pattern). [oracle: bun test]
When the injected auth-check reports authenticated (backend=codex), dispatch proceeds unchanged. [oracle: bun test]
When backend=claude, no codex preflight runs and the dispatch path is byte-identical (auth-check never invoked, no early return). [oracle: bun test]
The preflight logic is the shared fn from US-001, not duplicated inline at each site. [oracle: grep -q 'codexAuthPreflight' src/supervisor/loop.ts]
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck). [oracle: bun run typecheck]
Tests pass (bun test). [oracle: bun test]
Lint/static spine passes (bun run check:all). [oracle: bun run check:all]
userStories.notes: Sites: src/supervisor/loop.ts (~line 1167, implementer, implBackend/implModel already resolved), src/supervisor/review.ts (~line 391, reviewer, reviewBackend/reviewModel already resolved), src/supervisor/plan-runner.ts (~line 596 planner and ~line 636 auditor, backend/model already resolved). Model the abort on the existing container-mode fail-closed early-returns: loop.ts returns { status: 'blocked', ... } with a named reason without dispatching (see loop.ts finishTerminal + the container-reason blocked returns ~lines 459-483, 924); review.ts returns { status: 'error', detail } (~line 381). Inject the auth-check as a DI dependency (do NOT hardcode a real codex subprocess in these fns) so unit tests can drive authenticated/unauthenticated without spawning codex. Existing test files touching these: test/supervisor/events.test.ts, test/supervisor/plan/plan-runner.test.ts. Keep emitSpawnResolution calls as-is (they are separate from the preflight). Grep patterns.md for 'container' fail-closed precedent.

userStories.title: Wire fail-closed preflight at the run.ts orchestrator dispatch site
userStories.description: As `cam run`, I need the codex auth preflight enforced before the orchestrator respawn-pane so that selecting backend=codex for the orchestrator while codex is unauthenticated halts bootstrap with an actionable error instead of launching a doomed orchestrator pane.
acceptanceCriteria: run.ts orchestrator dispatch runs codexAuthPreflight (with the production auth-check) immediately before its respawn-pane call. [oracle: grep -q 'codexAuthPreflight' src/commands/run.ts]

When backend=codex and the injected auth-check reports unauthenticated, run.ts halts the orchestrator bootstrap with an actionable error naming `codex login` and never respawns the orchestrator pane. [oracle: bun test]
When the injected auth-check reports authenticated (backend=codex), the orchestrator dispatch proceeds unchanged. [oracle: bun test]
When backend=claude, the run.ts dispatch path is byte-identical (auth-check never invoked). [oracle: bun test]
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck). [oracle: bun run typecheck]
Tests pass (bun test). [oracle: bun test]

userStories.notes: Site: src/commands/run.ts (~line 441, orchestrator dispatch; orchModel/orchBackend already resolved). The orchestrator respawn-pane -k is at ~line 458. Abort BEFORE that respawn: surface an actionable printError (naming `codex login`) and return a non-zero exit, mirroring how run.ts already fails bootstrap for other preconditions. Inject the auth-check for testability so tests never spawn real codex. Keep the emitSpawnResolution call as-is. Reuse the shared codexAuthPreflight from US-001.
